history.p: The ‘sinfonia a 16’ has a somewhat unusual orchestration and is more similar to a concerto for trumpet than the traditional sinfonia. Also Johann Gottlieb Graun, a contemporary of Scheibe’s, whom he knew and admired, wrote a ‘sinfonia a 16’ (1768) with a similar instrumentation. The present transcription of Scheibe's work was carried out by the professional copyist Johann Michael Baldauff whose hand is known from a vast number of works now located in Schwerin, Landesbibliothek Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Baldauff produced transcripts of works by composers such as Georg Philipp Telemann, Adolph Carl Kunzen, Baldassare Galuppi, Carl Heinrich Graun, as well as composers who worked in Copenhagen during the middle and the end of the eighteenth century, including Giuseppe Sarti, Paolo Scalabrini, Claus Nielsen Schall and also the present work of Scheibe's. Baldauff was active in the years 1748–80 and might have obtained or gained access to a collection of works associated with Copenhagen during his early active years.

physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format, placed in limp folder with instrumental parts; music (fols. 1r–21r), pages numbered 1–41 in pencil in library hand, blank page; in all 22 folios. Hand-ruled paper: first movement has 14 staves on pp. 1–8 and 15 staves on pp. 9–16 (10 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink; pp. 17–24 originally with 12 staves, later one added at top and bottom of page. Second and third movements have 20 staves on pp. 25–26, 28–34, 37–40, 19 staves on p. 27 and 21 staves on pp. 35–36, 41 (8 mm; single rastrum used) in darker brown as well as light-brown ink and music in black ink. Various blank staves on each page. A clean copy with few alterations; a few crosses in pencil at various bar lines suggests that a transcript was made from the present score; also bar numbers added in pencil. The transcript was most likely produced sometime between 1750 and 1770.

Two paper types of a fairly dense quality: One for the first movement which normally was employed for instrumental parts and a different one for the remaining two movements (normally used for scores). Limp folder, including both score and parts, has 'Scheibe' in ink and label with '4852' (in red) pasted on spine; several markings and additions in pencil, in library hand.
Source consists of 16 parts (clrno.1 conc., clrno.2, princ., timp., 2 cor., fl. obl., 2 fl., 2 ob., vl.1, vl.2, va., fg., bc.) The material was most likely produced sometime between 1750 and 1770.
